title: I pulled my sister's wedding speech after I read the draft
hook: My sister's wedding speech mentioned my ex by name three times, so I told her she wasn't giving it.
narration: My sister's wedding speech mentioned my ex by name three times, so I told her she wasn't giving it. I'd found the draft open on her laptop the night before. Jokes about my old boyfriend. A line about how I always pick the wrong one. I didn't shout. I just said, you're not speaking tomorrow. She went quiet, closed the laptop, and left. At the reception my maid of honour handed me a folded page. My sister's real speech. It was about our mum, who died in March, and how she'd promised to walk me down the aisle in her place. The laptop draft was the joke version she'd written to make me laugh. She'd rehearsed the real one forty times. She sat at table nine and didn't look up once. So. Do I apologise, or was I right to check?
verdict: You were right to read it. You were wrong to decide before you asked.
